full_judgment:
4. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit in part, that is, allowed the claim of the plaintiff to the tune of TK. 4,13,899.00. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said part decree the plaintiff filed Artha Rin Appeal No.1 of 2004 before the District Judge, Rajbari. The appeal was heard by the learned District Judge himself who by the judgment and decree dated 05.07.2005 dismissed the appeal affirming those passed by the trial Court. Against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court the plaintiff-petitioner filed Civil Revision No.5201 of 2005 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the civil revision by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule affirming those of the appellate Court. 

 6. From, the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned Judges refused to interfere with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court on the ground that the appellate Court concurred with the findings of the trial Court on proper consideration of the exhibits. The learned, Judges further found that on perusal of the evidence, they did not find any reason to "negate" the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the appellate Court in exercising jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
